notes: SCOPE TEST (decisive): q="Savio" against pool project 379335744 and against unrelated project 379335189 ("JD RCA Flaky Samples") returned byte-for-byte identical results - same 2 users (id 3325 "User D", id 4650 "User D Test"), same group_id 2615, same full payload. This confirms the capability's own guidance: despite the path param and the name, project_id resolves the route only and is never used in the lookup - the search is group-scoped (caller's group 2615), not project-scoped. Like its sibling get_project_users_v2_v1, the 'project users' naming is nominal here too; the precedent from search_group_tags (genuinely group-scoped, contrary to the user-listing siblings) does NOT extend to this capability - it lands with the other nominally-project-scoped user listings, making this the fourth user-listing capability confirmed to ignore project_id in its filter. DRIFT is scoped narrowly to the response schema: the 200 schema's user item `properties` omits `email`, `is_re_arch_enabled`, and `is_test_plan_detailed_report_enabled`, but all three are returned on every row in both live calls. Notably this is a prose-vs-schema split where prose is the one that's right: the capability's own flat top-level `returns` list (outside the expanded JSON schema) already names all three fields correctly - only the expanded 200 schema's `properties` block under-declares them. All required fields (id, full_name, onboarded, group_id, browserstack_user_id, role, has_access, permissions) were present on both rows, so no declared_missing. info.count (2) matched len(users) (2) exactly - no count-vs-rows disagreement here, and next:null is correct since count < page_size (30), so no second page existed to walk. No error responses were encountered (both attempts succeeded on the first try), so no error-envelope comparison applies and none was attempted.
